answer: A mechanism that actually bites: require a sealed latency proof from the identity's own host, because jetty only stays cheap while a datacenter running 500 clones shows one shared timing fingerprint and gets clustered. Concretely, copper is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any dune approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
